cover_letter.subject: Application for Test Engineer Electrolysis
paragraphs: Your posting asks for an engineer who can assemble laboratory cells, execute test protocols and turn measurements into clear results. That is the work I have done every week for the last two years, first on lithium-ion cells and now on fuel cell stacks at Example Energy GmbH, and I would like to bring it to your electrolysis test team.

At Example Energy I built a standalone fuel cell test bench with PLC control and Python logging. I used it to run polarization curves on 12 stacks and wrote the start-stop cycling procedures that shortened a full test campaign from six weeks to four. Electrolysis cells differ from fuel cells in their operating point, but the discipline is the same: a stable bench, a written protocol and data that another engineer can trust.

Data analysis is the part of testing I enjoy most. I analyse voltage decay in Python and present degradation trends to our design team every week, which has taught me to report what the data shows and to say plainly what it does not show. As a working student I also automated battery test reports with pandas, which saved about three hours per test series.

I have not yet worked on electrolyzers, and I would say so openly in an interview. What I can offer from the first week is careful bench work, reliable procedures and analysis that helps your developers decide faster. My German is at B2 level and I use it daily with technicians.
I would welcome the chance to discuss how my testing experience can support Example Hydrogen. Thank you for considering my application.
